title: Curri launches same-day delivery at checkout
summary: Curri for eCommerce adds same-day delivery to online checkout for distributors and retailers, from small boxes to flatbed loads, with a live price upfront.
body_markdown:
[Curri for eCommerce](https://www.curri.com/ecommerce) puts same-day delivery in any online checkout. Distributors and retailers can offer buyers a same-day option for any order size, from a small box to a flatbed load, with a live price shown before the buyer pays. Curri matches each order to the right vehicle and sends a driver to the store or branch that holds the inventory.


The Curri API is live today and already used by major nationwide retailers. Curri moves nearly 40K deliveries a month, and over 35% are more than 150 lbs.


## Why does same-day delivery for distributors belong in checkout?


Buyers already shop online. In[BigCommerce's 2025 Industrial Buyer Report](https://www.bigcommerce.com/resources/2025-industrial-buyer-report/) , 62% of buyers of electrical, HVAC and industrial supply products said they purchase online.


Urgent and heavy orders are the exception. When a contractor needs materials on the jobsite today, the website stops being an option and the phone takes over, because a standard checkout offers ground shipping or in-store pickup and little in between. Curri closes that gap, and the[full explainer on same-day delivery at checkout](https://www.curri.com/blog/same-day-delivery-at-checkout) walks through how.


## What does Curri for eCommerce show the buyer at checkout?


A same-day option sits beside the shipping choices a buyer already knows. Curri calculates the price live from the items, the store and the address, so the buyer sees the cost and the delivery window before paying.


A buyer picks same-day delivery at checkout, then follows the driver on a live map.


The distributor decides how that price shows. It can appear as a line item, sit inside the product price, or drop to free over a threshold.


One API call returns live prices for rush, same-day and scheduled delivery, so you can offer buyers the speed they need right at checkout. The API can be configured to show whichever delivery options you want, by location, by item, or based on your own internal fleet's availability.


## How does Curri deliver big and bulky same-day orders?


Curri matches every order to a vehicle by weight and dimensions, from a car to a flatbed, and dispatches a driver to the store. The network behind it includes 16K+ carriers and 56 vehicle and accessory options. For on-demand retail orders, the median time from booking to a driver at pickup is 34 minutes. It is the same on-demand network behind[Curri Hotshots](https://www.curri.com/hotshots) , now reachable from a checkout button.


Buyers follow the delivery with live tracking and an ETA. Photo proof of delivery flows back into the distributor's order system and customer notifications, so a missing-order call becomes one screen instead of a hunt through a carrier portal.


For the full picture, see how[Curri's platform matches shipments with the right vehicle type](https://www.curri.com/blog/how-curris-platform-matches-retail-shipments-with-the-right-vehicle-type) and why[GPS tracking and proof of delivery](https://www.curri.com/blog/gps-tracking-pod-visibility-retail-van-fleet-delivery) matter for every drop.


Want to see it on your own catalog?[Plan a same-day pilot](https://www.curri.com/ecommerce/pilot) and Curri will walk through your markets and categories.


## How do distributors connect the same-day delivery API?


Teams with a web developer can use the[Curri API](https://docs.curri.com/) today to add same-day delivery to a custom storefront, with a sandbox to test before going live.


[Curri Embed](https://www.curri.com/ecommerce) , a checkout component Curri renders under the distributor's brand, is in development with design partners now and rolls out in Q4. Curri also plans apps for Shopify, Adobe Commerce, BigCommerce, NetSuite and Salesforce Commerce.
